questions.question: Suggest suitable model materials for each part of the stairs and ramp at 1:20 and explain how the conversion table is produced and used.
questions.expected_answer: Concrete slab, steps and landing: thick card, foam board or mounting board; fill under the ramp: polystyrene blocks or stacked card; rails and posts: 3 to 4 millimetre dowel or stiff wire; kerb: card strip; ground: a hardboard base about 700 by 300; brushed surface: fine sandpaper or sandy paint; realistic grey and metal colours. The conversion table lists every dimension from the working drawing divided by 20, for example rise 600 to 30, riser 150 to 7.5, ramp leg 7 200 to 360, rail 900 to 45, post spacing 1 500 to 75; it is checked by a second team member, pinned at the bench, and every part is marked out from it and labelled before cutting.

questions.question: State the safe working rules for the craft knife and the hot glue gun, and describe how dust, mess and injuries are handled.
questions.expected_answer: Craft knife: cut only on a cutting mat, keep fingers well back on the rule, cut away from the body in several light passes, cap or retract the blade when put down, change blades as soon as they drag, dispose of blades in a marked container. Hot glue gun: rest it on its stand, hold parts with tweezers or scrap card not fingers, keep a bowl of cold water on the bench and plunge any burn in it at once, switch off and unplug when not in use. Sand gently in a ventilated room and wipe dust rather than blowing it; keep the bench tidy; return tools, count blades and sweep at the end; report every cut or burn to the teacher immediately.

questions.question: Describe the order in which the model is built, where checks are made, and what records are kept for the Make assessment.
questions.expected_answer: Mark out the plan on the base from the table; cut ramp legs, landing and kerbs and check the leg length gives 1 in 12 before gluing; build the fill and glue the ramp surface, taped flat; cut the four steps and check all risers are equal before gluing; fit the landing level and flat; mark and drill post holes at scaled spacing, fit posts cut to 45 plus fixing, checking each is vertical and the right height; glue handrails along the tops extending beyond the ends, add braces; paint, texture the walking surfaces and add a door and a scale figure. Records: the final specification check sheet with ticks and the photographs of the model from front, top and side matching the drawing's views, filed in the PAT file.
